provenance.method: ran the reference prepare_audio_segments with duration probing and ffmpeg slicing stubbed, so the arithmetic is pinned without needing real media
provenance.note: duration probing and slicing shell out to ffmpeg/ffprobe; the native body needs an equivalent. What this pins is the SEGMENT ARITHMETIC and the failure dispositions.

rules.count: ceiling division of duration by 300, floored at 1 for very short audio

exactly_one_chunk.label: 2 minutes -> one segment, last chunk is the remainder

zero_duration_floors_to_one.label: zero duration still yields one segment

collision_deconfliction.note: ⛔ THIS IS A RANDOM WALK, NOT A DECREMENT. An earlier capture of this oracle recorded ONE draw (120000_299) and it was written up as a rule. It is one of four roughly-equal outcomes.
collision_deconfliction.mechanism: each attempt picks at random WHICH component to change (time or duration) and at random WHETHER to add or subtract one; on collision it walks again from the new value, up to a bounded number of attempts, so the key can drift far from the original
collision_deconfliction.why_it_matters: the time component moves MORE OFTEN than the duration, so the key most often misreports the segment's START TIME — and in a journal keyed on day+time that is worse than a wrong duration. An earlier write-up analysed only the duration axis.
collision_deconfliction.and_the_duration_field_already_lies_with: the key's duration component is the CONSTANT 300 for every chunk, so the last chunk of essentially every import is misdescribed by its own key regardless of collisions
collision_deconfliction.how_to_test: ⛔ do not assert a specific deconflicted key. Assert the PROPERTY: after deconfliction the segment's true start time and true duration are both recoverable from data written beside it, not from the key.

fractional_durations.note: ⛔ the count is int((duration + 299) // 300), which is NOT ceiling division for FRACTIONAL durations — and real duration probes always return fractions. The last chunk absorbs duration minus its offset and CAN EXCEED 300s.
fractional_durations.why_it_matters: every other case in this oracle uses an integer duration, so a port that clamps the last chunk to 300 or truncates the duration to whole seconds passes all of them and silently drops the tail of the recording, reporting zero dropped chunks.
